summaries.beginner: In the roundworm, turning on one cell and watching the others shows that activity does not simply follow the known wiring diagram. Some signals travel without a direct synapse, using secreted peptides, and that extra wireless layer helps predict spontaneous brain activity.
summaries.intermediate: Posted on arXiv (2022), Randi, Sharma, Dvali, and Leifer measure signal propagation in 23,427 neuron pairs in the C. elegans head using optogenetic activation and whole-brain calcium imaging, reporting sign, strength, temporal properties, and causal direction. They find functional propagation differs from anatomical predictions; mutant experiments implicate extrasynaptic signaling, including dense-core-vesicle-dependent events on seconds-or-less timescales that often lack a direct wired connection. The measured atlas predicts spontaneous activity better than anatomy. Discussion frames extrasynaptic peptides as evoking acute transients, not only slow modulation, and stresses that the atlas reports effective, not necessarily direct, connections.
summaries.advanced: The extract does not give a numeric improvement for spontaneous-activity prediction. The 23,427 figure is pairs tested, not confirmed connections. Nuclear calcium indicators omit compartmentalized dynamics; observed transients are slow. Catalog journal metadata are empty; this is the arXiv version (2022, updated 2023). Comparisons to anatomy use connectome-constrained simulations of effective connections as described in the discussion.

plain_language_summary: In the roundworm, turning on one cell and watching the others shows that activity does not simply follow the known wiring diagram. Some signals travel without a direct synapse, using secreted peptides, and that extra wireless layer helps predict spontaneous brain activity.

ocar.opportunity: A complete cellular catalogue of the adult Drosophila central nervous system (around 150,000 neurons) is imminent. Grouping neurons into types (1–1,000 cells per hemisphere) is needed to parse complexity. Matched transcriptomic and morphological types could integrate connectomics and enable functional predictions from wiring diagrams.
ocar.challenge: Complexity is still hard to parse without consistent types. Matching morphological and transcriptomic definitions brain-wide remains incomplete.
ocar.action: Bates, Janssens, Jefferis, and Aerts, in Current Opinion in Neurobiology (2019), review how neuroanatomical and gene-expression data are being used to discover neuronal types at scale, emphasizing correlation among lineage, gene expression, morphology, connectivity, response properties, and shared behavioural significance.
ocar.resolution: Initial studies comparing morphological and transcriptomic definitions of neuronal type suggest these are highly consistent, but there is much to do to match the approaches brain-wide. Matched single-cell transcriptomic and morphological data are presented as an effective reference point to integrate other data types, including connectomics, enhancing functional predictions from wiring diagrams and facilitating molecular genetic manipulation of types.
ocar.future_work: Matching morphological and transcriptomic definitions brain-wide, and using matched single-cell data as a reference to integrate connectomics and genetic manipulation.

summaries.beginner: The adult fruit fly has on the order of 150,000 central neurons, too many to think about one by one. This review discusses how anatomy and gene expression together define cell types, which then become the units for wiring diagrams and genetic tools.
summaries.intermediate: In Current Opinion in Neurobiology (2019), Bates, Janssens, Jefferis, and Aerts review neuronal cell-type discovery in Drosophila as a complete cellular catalogue of the adult central nervous system (around 150,000 neurons) nears. They treat type as a bundle of co-varying properties—lineage, gene expression, morphology, connectivity, response properties, and behavioural role—with 1–1,000 cells per hemisphere. They report that initial comparisons of morphological and transcriptomic types look highly consistent, but brain-wide matching remains to be done, and they argue matched single-cell data will integrate connectomics and aid genetic manipulation.
summaries.advanced: The on-disk PDF was a mismatch and could not be replaced, so this card follows the catalog abstract. The 150,000-neuron figure is a 2019 estimate. No specific datasets, clustering metrics, or type counts are given. “Highly consistent” is qualitative.

plain_language_summary: The adult fruit fly has on the order of 150,000 central neurons, too many to think about one by one. This review discusses how anatomy and gene expression together define cell types, which then become the units for wiring diagrams and genetic tools.
